lesson_title: The Tax Office in the Sky
hook_text: Throw a ball straight up. At the very top its speed is zero — so is the acceleration zero too?
clip_script: Throw a ball straight up at 29,4 metres per second and watch gravity run the most predictable tax office on Earth: every second, it deducts 9,8 from your speed. One second in, you're doing 19,6. Two seconds, 9,8. Three seconds — zero. The ball hangs at the top of its flight, perfectly still for one instant. Now the question that catches thousands of students: at that frozen moment, is the acceleration zero too? No. The tax office does not close just because your balance hits zero. The acceleration is 9,8 metres per second squared, downward, for the entire flight — on the way up, at the top, on the way down. And because the tax rate never changes, the descent is the climb played in reverse: three seconds up, three seconds down, and the ball lands back in your hand at exactly 29,4 — the speed you launched it with. Time up equals time down. Speed at any height going up equals speed at that height coming down. Know half the flight and physics hands you the other half free. That mirror, plus three equations, is the entire topic — the most predictable calculation in the subject.
visual_style: A ball climbing in slow motion beside a ticking speed counter that drains by 9,8 each second, freezing at the top with a bold 'v = 0, a = 9,8' stamp, then the footage running literally in reverse as the counter refills to 29,4.
mood: Calm and confident — a famous trick question defused in real time.
pacing: Steady climb with the draining counter, dramatic freeze at the top, satisfying mirrored descent, quick close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and own the most predictable calculation in physics.
